raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview MRV2 captures CUDA graphs with the `input_ids` buffer even when `execute_model` passes `input_ids=None` alongside `inputs_embeds`. With breakable CUDA graphs and DEBUG logging, the replay address check then fails on the first PIECEWISE replay of a multimodal or prompt-embeds model. This PR applies `execute_model`'s rule at capture. Same block as #61016. ## Claims - MRV2, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`, `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, a model that runs with `inputs_embeds` and does not set `requires_raw_input_tokens`: the first breakable PIECEWISE replay no longer fails `Input tensor addresses changed between capture and replay`. - Capture now calls the model with the same `input_ids` / `inputs_embeds` combination as serving, for FULL graphs too. Greedy output unchanged on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` (text and image requests, breakable and default graphs), MI355X. - Unchanged: models with `requires_raw_input_tokens`, model states that supply `inputs_embeds` through their own inputs (`DiffusionGemmaModelState`, `LongcatNgramModelState`), text-only models without prompt embeds, non-first PP ranks, MRV1. ## Validation **Unit test.** `test_capture_input_ids_match_execute_model` (`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py`) runs `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture` on CPU with a recording model and checks whether the captured call gets `input_ids`, for four cases: a multimodal / prompt-embeds state, a raw-token model, a state without `dummy_inputs_embeds`, and `uses_inputs_embeds=False`. It runs in the CPU `v1` step (`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml:330`). ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py -k test_capture_input_ids_match_execute_model -rA ``` - With this PR: `4 passed`. - On the base commit: all 4 fail with `TypeError: ModelCudaGraphManager.capture() got an unexpected keyword argument 'uses_inputs_embeds'`. - With the new argument but without the capture rule, only the multimodal case fails: `assert (tensor([0, 0, 0, 0], dtype=torch.int32) is not None) == False`. Dropping any one condition of the rule fails exactly the case for that condition; keying the rule on `inputs_embeds` being in the capture inputs fails the case without `dummy_inputs_embeds` and the `uses_inputs_embeds=False` case. - Rest of the file on CPU-only torch 2.14.1: unchanged from the base (`test_full_capture_sets_graph_pool_id_before_cuda_graph` fails on both with `Fail to set current stream`; no accelerator for the conftest teardown). - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `typos`: clean. `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11` on the changed files: no new errors. **Serving.** - Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-e4a5b5537344b103ed10de7764378ef09604ef3d`, whose `cudagraph_utils.py`, `model_runner.py`, `breakable_cudagraph.py` and `model_states/` equal this PR's base; patched arm with this PR's `vllm/` changes applied. - AMD Instinct MI355X, TP1, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` at revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`, one text request and one image request (a red square), greedy, 64 tokens. ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct --revision 66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3 \ --max-model-len 4096 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "max_cudagraph_capture_size": 512}' ``` The INFO rows use `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO`; the default-graph row also sets `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`. | Configuration | Base | This PR | |---|---|---| | Breakable, DEBUG | text request HTTP 500, then the engine stops (image request HTTP 500) | text and image HTTP 200 | | Breakable, INFO: greedy text / image | — | identical to base / identical to base | | Default graphs (`torch.compile`), INFO: greedy text / image | — | identical to base / identical to base; graph capture 3.98 + 4.07 GiB in both arms | - Base failure, on the first replay (the 24-token text prefill): `AssertionError: Input tensor addresses changed between capture and replay for BatchDescriptor(num_tokens=24, num_reqs=None, uniform=False, has_lora=False, num_active_loras=0). Expected [137316278489088, 137312627759104, 137296458285056], got [137312627759104, 137296458285056].` The missing address is the first one (`input_ids`). - This PR, same launch: no such line; answers "Red, blue, and yellow are the three primary colors." and "The image shows a square with a red color." - Not run: a prompt-embeds model (`--enable-prompt-embeds`). ## Details - **Root cause.** On the first PP rank, `execute_model` sets `input_ids = None` when `uses_inputs_embeds` is set, the model state returned an `inputs_embeds` tensor, and the model does not set `requires_raw_input_tokens` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1970-1996`). `ModelCudaGraphManager.capture` built its inputs with `input_buffers.input_ids` and only dropped them on later PP ranks (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py:688-698`). `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper` collects the tensor kwargs at capture and, at DEBUG, compares them with the replay call's (`vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py:361-364`, `:421-427`), so it sees one more tensor at capture (`input_ids`) than at replay. The others keep their addresses; the check fails because the lists differ. - **Fix.** Capture applies the same rule. The runner passes `uses_inputs_embeds`, and the model state's `dummy_inputs_embeds` decides, as in `execute_model`'s dummy run. Keying on whether the capture inputs contain `inputs_embeds` would be wrong for `DiffusionGemmaModelState` and `LongcatNgramModelState`, which add `inputs_embeds` in `prepare_dummy_inputs` and `prepare_inputs` while `execute_model` keeps `input_ids` for them. - **FULL graphs.** The change applies to FULL captures as well, which also replay with whatever the capture traced. A model whose forward reads `input_ids` when given `inputs_embeds` without setting `requires_raw_input_tokens` already gets `input_ids=None` in eager, PIECEWISE and startup profiling runs (`profile_run` → `_dummy_run` → `execute_model(dummy_run=True)`), so capture now traces the path those runs take. DBO capture is covered by the same change; `slice_model_inputs` skips `None` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ubatch_utils.py:246-249`). - **Alternatives.** Skipping kwargs that are `None` at replay in the DEBUG check would hide a tensor that a captured segment read at capture and replay no longer passes. Excluding `input_ids` in `_replay` would copy a model-runner rule into compilation code and leave capture and serving on different Python paths. - **MRV1** is not affected: its capture dummy run uses `_prepare_mm_inputs`, which drops `input_ids` the same way (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:3247-3256`, `:5719-5727`). - **Default users.** On CUDA, several multimodal architectures enable breakable graphs by default (`default_breakable_cudagraph_architectures`), so DEBUG logging alone reaches the check for those that do not set `requires_raw_input_tokens`. Not run on CUDA. This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

files.patch:
@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
 from collections import defaultdict
-from contextlib import contextmanager
+from contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
 
@@ -308,6 +308,77 @@ def capture(self, create_forward_fn, progress_bar_desc):
         assert call.args[0].max_query_len == expected_max_query_len
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "uses_inputs_embeds,state_embeds,raw_tokens,keeps_input_ids",
+    [
+        (True, True, False, False),
+        (True, True, True, True),
+        (True, False, False, True),
+        (False, True, False, True),
+    ],
+)
+def test_capture_input_ids_match_execute_model(
+    monkeypatch, uses_inputs_embeds, state_embeds, raw_tokens, keeps_input_ids
+):
+    """Capture must pass input_ids exactly when execute_model does; the
+    breakable graph's DEBUG check compares the two calls' tensor arguments."""
+    num_tokens = 4
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_cudagraph_utils,
+        "get_pp_group",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(is_first_rank=True, is_last_rank=True),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_cudagraph_utils.current_platform, "get_global_graph_pool", lambda: object()
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_cudagraph_utils, "prepare_inputs_to_capture", lambda *a, **kw: ({}, {})
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_cudagraph_utils, "set_forward_context", lambda *a, **kw: nullcontext()
+    )
+    desc = BatchExecutionDescriptor(CUDAGraphMode.FULL, num_tokens, num_tokens)
+
+    def capture(self, create_forward_fn, progress_bar_desc):
+        create_forward_fn(desc, warmup=False)(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_cudagraph_utils.CudaGraphManager, "capture", capture)
+
+    embeds = torch.zeros(num_tokens, 8)
+    # A state without dummy_inputs_embeds supplies inputs_embeds only through
+    # its own inputs, so execute_model keeps input_ids.
+    model_state = SimpleNamespace(
+        prepare_dummy_inputs=lambda num_reqs, n: {"inputs_embeds": embeds[:n]},
+        dummy_inputs_embeds=lambda n: embeds[:n] if state_embeds else None,
+    )
+    calls = []
+
+    class Model:
+        requires_raw_input_tokens = raw_tokens
+
+        def __call__(self, **kwargs):
+            calls.append(kwargs)
+            return torch.zeros(num_tokens, 8)
+
+    manager = gpu_cudagraph_utils.ModelCudaGraphManager(
+        _create_vllm_config(), torch.device("cpu"), CUDAGraphMode.FULL, 1
+    )
+    manager.capture(
+        Model(),
+        model_state,
+        InputBuffers(num_tokens, num_tokens, torch.device("cpu")),
+        None,
+        MagicMock(),
+        [],
+        KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=0, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[]),
+        uses_inputs_embeds=uses_inputs_embeds,
+    )
+
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+    assert (calls[0]["input_ids"] is not None) == keeps_input_ids
+    assert calls[0]["inputs_embeds"] is not None
+
+
 _DECODE_QUERY_LEN = 3

@@ -624,6 +624,7 @@ def capture(
         use_aux_hidden_state_outputs: bool = False,
         lora_capture_hook: Callable[[int, int, int], None] | None = None,
         progress_bar_desc: str = "Capturing CUDA graphs",
+        uses_inputs_embeds: bool = False,
     ) -> None:
         """Capture CUDA graphs for model forward pass."""
         self.use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = use_aux_hidden_state_outputs
@@ -698,6 +699,14 @@ def create_forward_fn(
                 model_inputs["inputs_embeds"] = None
                 assert intermediate_tensors is not None
                 model_inputs["intermediate_tensors"] = intermediate_tensors[:num_tokens]
+            elif (
+                uses_inputs_embeds
+                and model_state.dummy_inputs_embeds(num_tokens) is not None
+                and not requires_raw_input_tokens(model)
+            ):
+                # Same rule as GPUModelRunner.execute_model, so capture passes
+                # the inputs that replay passes.
+                model_inputs["input_ids"] = None
 
             if desc.num_ubatches > 1:
                 # Prepare and park threads before capture; finish runs inside it.

@@ -1120,6 +1120,7 @@ def capture_model(self, *, profile_only: bool = False) -> int:
                         lora_capture_hook=create_lora_capture_hook(
                             self.lora_config, self
                         ),
+                        uses_inputs_embeds=self.uses_inputs_embeds,
                     )
                     self.model_state.capture_inner_cudagraphs(
                         input_buffers,
